source.title: When Source-Free Domain Adaptation Meets Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: L. Yi; Ge-Zheng Xu; Pengcheng Xu; Jiaqi Li; Rui-Zhi Pu; Charles Ling; A. McLeod; Bo-Yu Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no apparent cutoff or garbling affects the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training dynamics on source-model-generated noisy labels and reports target accuracy against ground truth, addressing early learning before label memorization. Its SFDA setting and noisy labels differ from the claim’s standard deep-network random-label setup.
record.gate_note: The paper studies source-free domain adaptation, where a pretrained source model assigns pseudo-labels to unlabeled target images. Figure 2 reports training-accuracy curves for CE, GCE, and ELR; Appendix H contrasts source-model-generated unbounded noise with bounded random label noise. Cited results from prior work are not extracted as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study reports early improvement against ground truth followed by noisy-label memorization in pretrained networks adapting to a new domain. These results test V6 in a new setting with source-generated pseudo-label noise.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that early-time learning persists under SFDA's unbounded pseudo-label noise and that ELR can exploit it to reduce memorization and improve adaptation. They also conclude that conventional bounded-noise robust losses cannot adequately address this noise.
record.recipe_differences: The study adapts pretrained source models on unlabeled target-domain images with source-model pseudo-labels; it does not use the original random-label image-classification setup. It measures target prediction accuracy over training and compares source-model-generated noise with bounded random noise.
record.method_sensitivity: Memorization speed differs between unbounded source-model-generated noise and bounded random label noise; the paper also says speed varies across datasets, with DomainNet slower than other datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: ELR preserves useful early predictions and reduces noisy-label memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early-learning regularization can reduce pseudo-label memorization during source-free domain adaptation.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4.1 bounds early ground-truth accuracy on mislabeled samples for logistic gradient descent on a linear classifier under a Gaussian-mixture model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear classifiers can recover signal early under the specified instance-dependent noise model, with at most half the samples mislabeled and sufficiently small cluster variance.

record.problems: The real-world learning-curve results are presented as figures without numerical curve values or uncertainty estimates. The experiments use domain-shifted pseudo-labels rather than fully random labels on the original training images.
record.rows_left_out: No results left out; Figure 2 and Appendix H comparisons are recorded as figure-only or qualitative text results because exact curve values are not stated.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time ratio for fitting random versus true labels and convergence across corruption fractions. Appendix H compares two noise mechanisms instead.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A corruption sweep from none to all, perfect training fit throughout, and steadily increasing test error.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after removing them.
A direct comparison of training from scratch on true versus completely random labels. The empirical tests use pretrained source models and partially incorrect target labels.

missing.what: CE and GCE early-learning dynamics on VisDA-C and Office-31, omitted from the Figure 2 rows.
Additional CE learning curves across all 12 DomainNet transfer tasks; Appendix F explicitly reports early accuracy improvement across these tasks.

record.verdict_notes: Fast memorization does not challenge V6, which specifies learning order without a minimum early-learning duration. No numerical curve values can be recovered from the supplied text. Eventual complete memorization is sometimes an expectation rather than a measured endpoint.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on completely random labels of the training images in the original settings, report test error at chance, or compare the same networks’ generalization on true labels.
Does not measure the training-time factor for fitting completely random versus true labels or sweep the fraction of corrupted labels.
Does not train on shuffled pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Does not sweep random corruption from none to all or report the corresponding training and test errors.
Does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or whether removing them changes generalization on true labels.
The noisy pseudo-labels are generated by source models under domain shift, rather than being a direct comparison of real labels with completely random labels in the original settings.

conditions.value: unbounded source-model-generated noise versus bounded random label noise

rows.measure: Prediction accuracy on target data during training
rows.baseline: Figure-only comparison between bounded random and unbounded source-model-generated noise
rows.value: Text states classifiers with unbounded noise start memorizing noisy labels within the first epoch; bounded-noise classifiers take more than a few epochs to start memorizing.
rows.note: The paper says first 90 steps are evaluated every batch, then every 0.3 epoch; no exact accuracy values are given.
rows.check: Specify that the bounded-noise comparison randomizes labels only on samples initially misclassified by the source model, leaving other labels unchanged. It is not completely random labeling of the dataset. The reported timing concerns the onset of memorization, not time to fit all noisy labels.

source_check.problem: The condition should specify that random replacements affect only target samples initially mislabeled by the source model. Timing describes memorization onset.
